chunks: And yet there are men who take others as compeers of God, and bestow on them love due to God; but the love of the faithful for God is more intense. If only the wicked could see now the agony that they will behold (on the Day of Resurrection), they will know that to God belongs the power entirely'. And the punishment of God is severe.

key_terms.أَنْدَادًا: Compeers or equals (used in the context of shirk)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the love of polytheists and the love of believers for God according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse distinguishes between 'equal love' (kushl) for idols and the 'superior love' (shadd al-hub) for Allah, emphasizing that true monotheism requires God to be the ultimate object of devotion. The phrase 'all power belongs to Allah' (al-quwwatu lillahi jami'an) is interpreted as a reminder that divine authority encompasses both the power to punish and the capacity to reward, serving as a deterrent for those who commit shirk. This realization on the Day of Judgment underscores the severity of injustice (zulm) in elevating created beings to the status of the Creator.
